Beard |asst_coach2=Mike Ekanem |asst_coach3=[[Hollis Price]] |asst_coach4=[[Kellen Sampson]] |stadium=[[Fertitta Center]] |champion= |tourney=[[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |tourney_result=Sweet Sixteen }} {{2025–26 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2025–26 Houston Cougars men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Houston]] in the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Cougars, led by 12th-year head coach [[Kelvin Sampson]], played their home games at the [[Fertitta Center]] as third-year members of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. ==Previous season== As the No. 1 seed in the [[2025 Big 12 men's basketball tournament]], held at [[T-Mobile Center]] in [[Kansas City, Missouri]], Houston received a bye to the quarterfinals. There, they defeated [[2024–25 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]], 77–68, to advance to the semifinals, where they would defeat [[2024–25 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|BYU]], 74–54, to advance to the championship game, where they would secure a 72–64 victory over [[2024–25 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]] to claim their first tournament title. As the tournament champion, Houston received an automatic bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2025 NCAA tournament]], ''also'' as the No. 1 seed. They were seeded in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Midwest regional – Indianapolis, Indiana|Midwest region]]. There, they defeated [[2024–25 SIU Edwardsville Cougars men's basketball team|SIU Edwardsville]], 78–40, in the First round, [[2024–25 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]], 81–76, in the Second round, [[2024–25 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], 62–60, in the Sweet Sixteen, and [[2024–25 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], 69–50, in the Elite Eight to advance to their first Final Four since 2021. In the Final Four, they overcame a 14-point deficit to defeat [[2024–25 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]], 70–67, to advance to their first [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship]] since [[1984 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|1984]]. In the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game]], despite leading for nearly the entire game – the same thing Duke did to them in the Final Four – Houston ultimately lost to [[2024–25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]], 65–63, denying them their first national title.{{Cite web |last=FOX 26 Digital |date=2025-04-07 |title=Houston Cougars lose
